conventions: cells lists every non-empty coordinate in row-major order: "at" is [x, y], then what is there plus a one-line description. This section alone fully describes the screen.
kind tile: art tile stamped at the cell.
kind static: fixed ASCII letter from the intrepid tileset (see fonts).
kind variable: dynamic digit cell; field names the value, place the digit (tens/ones/...). Values are right-aligned: the ones digit cell is fixed, the field grows left.
Two-row glyphs split into top/bottom halves; single-row glyphs use part "single".

Scenery rows 2-4 are positional slots (starting-point-*/destination-*, rows top/middle/bottom). The biome art comes from assets/travels/<biome>.json (grove 3x8 + vista 3x8 of existing tileset tiles); origin = route start, destination = route end, wiring picks the biome tileset per side (see scenery).

Journey chrome (box, icons, labels, progress markers) comes from assets/travel-tile.png (160x16 px, 20 cols x 2 rows) named by assets/travel-tileset.csv; "what" on chrome cells is the CSV name verbatim. Brown-top markers run on the origin half, grey-top on the destination half.

Forest ground uses the 3 travel floor icons (forest floor icon 1/2/3) for the forest biome as starter or destination; they are staged in the travel sheet (missing from the forest tileset) and get backported into forest gfx at wiring — assets/travels/forest.json keeps forest.* names until TILE ids exist.
Names follow the assets/*.csv style: lowercase words with spaces.
The mockup is a loose artist render, not pixel-exact: names describe INTENT per cell, the artist snaps art to the 8px grid when drawing.

fonts.intrepid: ASCII tileset assets/intrepid.png (16x6 sheet, chars 32-127), 1 tile per cell. Renders the 1-row TRAVELING... title. The artist may restyle glyphs; the wiring stays ASCII codes.
fonts.intrepid large: Double-height ASCII for SUPPLIES/stats (each glyph 2 cells tall). Not in intrepid.png yet: the artist extends the sheet with top/bottom halves per glyph (mockup shows tall narrow serif caps, digits and colon).

scenery.rule: Rows 2-4 form the journey strip. Cols 1-10 stamp the ORIGIN biome grove; cols 11-18 stamp the DESTINATION biome vista. Each journey route declares origin_biome/destination_biome (e.g. forest->desolate); tools/screen_compiler/travel_art_compile.py fetches assets/travels/<biome>.json for each side and emits a per-route strip table (src/game/travel_art_content.c). Horse, progress markers and all UI are journey chrome overlaid on top, not scenery.

forest.note: Forest grove + vista (see forest tileset). Ground cells use the 3 travel floor icons (forest floor icon 1/2/3, staged in the travel sheet) as starter or destination.

village.note: Orchard grove + rooftop vista to be drawn (see town tileset).

desolate.note: Dead scrub grove + boulder vista to be drawn (see desolate tileset).

snow.note: No current route ends in snow; mockup pair shows the snow vista. Sheet to be drawn when a snowy destination exists.

sheet.size: 3 rows x 8 cols of named tileset tiles per side (grove + vista) + 3 transition tiles
sheet.order: grove: origin arrangement cols 0-7; transition: one tile per row stamped in cols 8-9; vista: destination arrangement cols 10-17
sheet.palette: Tiles already live in the ROM tilesets; no new pixel art, no palette constraint beyond the source tileset.

chrome.size: 160x16 px = 20 columns x 2 rows of 8px tiles
chrome.note: Box chrome (10), single-tile icons (bow/bed/glass/map), label slices (HUNT 3 incl. T for hunt; REST 3 incl. T for rest; STUDY MAP 4; CONTINUE 4), B button, 3 forest floor icons, progress markers x2 sets (brown-top origin, grey-top destination: start/black empty/step/ending flag each). Brown ending-flag and grey start are spares for reversed legs.

palette.progress black: Brown-top markers on the origin half, grey-top on the destination half (start/black empty/step/ending flag per half).
